answer: Each agent locks a 60-credit reef bond for one stock lot, turning it over twice inside one tide window. A falcon auditor recomputes trades from the reef ledger, counting only trades with distinct counterparties, and burns bonds below the turnover bar. Turnover costs 30 in fees plus slippage of 1 per lot already sold in the window, so the k-th fake pays 60 plus 30+(k-1). One thousand fakes lock 60,000 and pay 529,500 in fees and slippage. A wash-trading ring fails because self-trades net to zero turnover. An honest agent posts 90 for one lot and recovers its 60 bond after a clean window.
